claim: Task wording flips rule versus family-resemblance categorisation: 'belongs to' gives more rule answers than 'is similar to'. The original (Norenzayan 2002, Study 2) and Many Labs 2 (N=7,396, d=0.86; rule 64% vs 44%) agree.
agent_test: Run the same classify task on the agent with 'belongs to' vs 'is similar to' wording at equal tokens; measure the rule-share shift. Use it to pick representation wording per task.
audit_note: Minor: in the original Study 2 European Americans did not shift with wording (rule 67% vs 69%); the flip was among East Asians, while Many Labs 2 reports the aggregate effect d=0.86 (rule 64% vs 44%), all numbers match.

claim: The claimed East Asian vs European American gap in rule use was not the replicated part of Norenzayan 2002. In Many Labs 2 the condition effect was d=0.86 overall, and the WEIRDness moderation ran opposite to the original (original European American d=0.00, East Asian d=0.67 for the condition effect).
agent_test: None needed for the agent. Treat 'East Asians use similarity' as unsupported for design.

claim: Norenzayan 2002 Study 1: when a rule conflicts with similarity to learned exemplars, East Asians made more extra errors, with equal learning ability. Klein 2009 found no culture differences in the rule condition across four countries and a difference only in response time in the similarity condition.
agent_test: Not needed.

claim: The belief-bias claim (Koreans worse on believable-conclusion syllogisms) was reduced to response bias by a reanalysis: Koreans were more conservative in saying 'valid'; no accuracy gap once bias is handled.
agent_test: Check agent syllogism errors for yes-rate bias before blaming belief bias; score with a bias-free measure.

claim: Focal vs context attention at eye level is mixed and stimulus-dependent. Chua 2005 (21 US, 24 Chinese) found Americans fixated the object 118 ms sooner (about g=0.72, 95% CI 0.12 to 1.33). Rayner 2007 (N=74) found no group difference over all scenes (background 2489 vs 2565 ms, F<1) but a partial effect on 6 Chua-like scenes (foreground 4299 vs 4813 ms, p=.04). Rayner 2009 (N=24) found nothing (all F<1). Goh 2009 (N=31) found longer US dwell and more Chinese object-background gaze shifts. A 7-sample 2025 study did not follow an East-West order.
agent_test: Eye-level attention has no agent analogue. Skip.

claim: Change blindness: East Asians find context changes faster and Americans find object changes faster, but from small samples (30-36 per group; Exp 1 interaction F(1,64)=3.96, p=.05) and mainly with culturally complex scenes (Exp 3 interaction F(1,58)=22.72). Same lab, no outside replication found.
agent_test: Show the agent an image or table with a focal vs a context change, with and without context-first prompting; compare detection. Low priority.

claim: Free recall of animated underwater scenes: Japanese gave about 70% more background statements and about 100% more relation statements; focal-fish mentions were equal. Original lab only; N not recorded in the reviews.
agent_test: No test; background only.

claim: The simple East-West axis for analytic vs holistic style did not hold in a preregistered 11-country study (N=993, Navon and embedded-figures): differences existed but not along East-West; individualism and long-term orientation related to both styles.
agent_test: None. Argues against hard-coding cultural personas into the schema.

claim: Other cross-cultural replications are weaker or reversed: in Klein 2009 the framed-line test favoured all three East Asian groups in both relative and absolute conditions (the original predicted an American advantage in the absolute one).
agent_test: None.

claim: Relational vs object bias in children is not a simple East-Asian pattern: Korean toddlers fall between US (object bias) and Chinese (relational bias), closer to US; Korean adults show no bias (52% relational, BF10=0.31).
agent_test: None.

claim: LLMs choose relational pairs on triads: GPT-3.5 0.87 and GPT-4 0.85 relational share (10 runs, 20 items), and holism scale scores above the human norm, stable across temperature 0 to 1.5 and prompt language. Gap check: Jin's 20-item test had only 10 real items; the items are published triads and no fresh-item control exists.
agent_test: Run a 20-triad test on our agent model; report relational share per run. Informational only: it shows the default representation bias.

claim: The LLM triad result depends on scoring and items: Hu 2026 finds the US model more relational than the Chinese model (R-C 8.10 vs 6.04, d=1.38) and no prompt-language effect (7.10 vs 7.04). The two studies do not directly conflict but are not comparable.
agent_test: If triads are used, fix one scoring rule up front.

claim: Prompt language (Chinese vs English) does not reliably shift LLM cultural tendencies. Sun and Wang's 8-model replication: Exp 1 language p=.15, d=.045; Exp 2 only 3 of 8 models significant, only qwen d=.54; Hu 2026 finds no language effect on triads. This contradicts Lu et al. (4-12 items, 2 models, seen only secondarily). Gap check: Lu et al. full text was not reachable (abstract only); the critique says it used 4 to 12 items per task, 2 models and unreleased items, so its numbers stay unverified.
agent_test: Check that prompt language or persona wording does not change agent answers on a fixed item set at temperature 0 and 1; if flat, drop persona and language prompts (supports G4 and 4b).
audit_note: Minor: Sun and Wang also report a small significant Exp 1 language effect within Chinese LLMs (p=.021); Lu et al. was not opened and the claim states that.

claim: Prompt framing (change-framed vs neutral) moves LLM output far more than prompt language: Sun and Wang Exp 1 framing d=-2.095 and eta-squared 0.54 vs language d=0.045. The summary table calls the framing effect 'small', which conflicts with the appendix. Related noise floor: formatting alone moves accuracy by a median 7.5 points (up to 76) in Sclar et al., and few-shot example composition moved Sabir's holistic share by up to 19 points.
agent_test: Use a framing manipulation as a control: any scaffold gain must beat the gain from re-wording at equal tokens.

claim: Generation probes of attention give inverted or mixed results in LLMs: the US image model drew more objects (11.53 vs 8.10, d=1.01) and placed horizons higher (533.5 vs 519.8) than the Chinese model; Chinese prompts gave more objects in generated landscapes (10.71 vs 8.91, d=0.49) but English prompts gave more objects in scene description (10.90 vs 10.06, d=0.36).
agent_test: None.

claim: Vision-language models write more holistic (background-first) captions for Japanese images and in Japanese. Image content is the larger factor: GPT4o-JP 26.10% holistic on COCO vs 73.37% on 1K Japanese photos (+47 points), plain GPT-4o already 57.6 to 59.1% on the Japanese set. Caption language is the smaller factor: on the same COCO images English original 12.34% vs Japanese translation 27.54% (+15.2), average translation shift 13.21%. The GPT-4o judge reads more holistic than humans (29.00% vs 17.75% for GPT4o-JP).
agent_test: None for a text agent.

claim: Models skew toward Western profiles: GPT models track US and Protestant European survey profiles (cultural prompting shrinks distance, e.g. GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65), VLMs do better on Western than East Asian images, and LLM word associations resemble US schemas.
agent_test: Not for the agent. Supports persona-free defaults and not trusting a model's self-reported culture.

claim: LLMs use both taxonomy and similarity when projecting properties, not one exclusive rule; text-trained static embeddings mostly encode thematic relations. Related (O7): in human story retrieval, surface similarity drives recall and relational structure drives soundness (Gentner 1993: quality of reminding 2.36 surface vs 1.48 analogy vs 0.86 relations-only).
agent_test: Test analogue retrieval (O7) with thematic vs taxonomic cues at equal tokens. Low priority.

claim: No study was found that runs child-style thematic vs taxonomic triads on LLMs against human age data (8 searches; APIs rate-limited, so absence is weak evidence).
agent_test: Open gap; cheap to run.

claim: Vision-language models carry both texture and shape cues; prompts alone move shape bias between 49% and 72%, and vision-side steering moves it more. An object-vs-surface bias can be steered by instruction.
agent_test: If vision input is used, test an instruction that names the relevant cue vs none.

claim: In face-recognition eye tracking, priming individualism or collectivism did not change eye movements (Gingras 2023, 15 Swiss and 21 Chinese participants), and most British-born Chinese kept Eastern strategies with about 25% using Western ones (Kelly 2011), so culture of origin alone does not determine strategy. Faces only.
agent_test: None. Supports not using collectivist role prompts to change attention style.
audit_note: Gingras 2023 shows only that a pronoun-priming manipulation (N=36) did not change eye movements, and its group differences replicated only partly, so it does not show social orientation fails to explain the differences; Kelly 2011 (about 25% Western, 30% in Exp 1) is correct.
claim_before_audit: Eye-tracking cultural differences are not explained by social orientation or by culture alone: priming individualism or collectivism did not change face eye movements (Gingras 2023), and about 25% of British-born Chinese used Western strategies (Kelly 2011). Faces only.

claim: Wording and format noise can be large relative to small effects: meaning-preserving prompt format changes give a median 7.5 point and up to 76 point accuracy spread (Sclar 2023); equivalent query rewrites give a 45.48 point best-worst win-rate gap on Llama-2-70B-chat (Cao 2024). Scaffold gains of only a few points should be checked against sampled paraphrases before being trusted.
agent_test: In each scaffold test, run at least 5 paraphrases of the task wording and report worst, best and mean; require the scaffold gain to exceed the paraphrase spread.
audit_note: Sclar and Cao report spreads (median 7.5 points, up to 76; best-worst gap 45.48 on AlpacaEval win-rate for Llama-2-70B-chat) but do not show that a scaffold gain under 7 to 10 points is indistinguishable from noise; that threshold is an extrapolation across different tasks and settings.
claim_before_audit: Wording and format noise is a large fraction of any small effect: meaning-preserving prompt format changes give a median 7.5 point and up to 76 point accuracy spread (Sclar 2023); equivalent query rewrites give a 45.48 point best-worst gap on Llama-2-70B-chat (Cao 2024). A scaffold gain below about 7 to 10 points is not distinguishable from wording noise unless paraphrases are sampled.

claim: An instruction to ignore irrelevant context gives a few points on distractor-heavy math (GSM-IC: CoT 72.4 to 77.8, least-to-most 77.5 to 80.6, zero-shot CoT 29.0 to 30.5; code-davinci-002). No study tested a 'context first' vs 'focal object first' instruction. Gap 3 is partly informed, not closed.
agent_test: Add a distractor-heavy set with focal-first, context-first and neutral instructions at equal tokens; compare accuracy.

claim: Human analogue retrieval is driven by surface similarity, not relational structure; relational-only matches were recalled least (quality 0.86 vs 2.36 surface vs 1.48 analogy) though judged sound (soundness 4.40 for analogies vs 2.80 surface). Secondhand LLM reports say models are also drawn to surface similarity in analogy tasks.
agent_test: For O7 retrieval, compare cues that name the relation or causal structure vs object-matched cues at equal tokens; measure whether the correct precedent is retrieved.

claim: The Lu et al. 2025 language effect could not be checked: only the abstract was reachable, items and prompts were not released, and the critique counts 4 to 12 items per task, 2 models and 1 of 7 tasks with non-public items. Open.
agent_test: Replicate on our model with our own fresh items at temperature 0 and 1, prompt language and persona varied.
